authorship: Developer-authored synthetic labels, not user-adjudicated study data or personal accuracy evidence.

pairs.left: For the parcel pilot, delivery succeeds when every package reaches its recipient within two days of dispatch.
pairs.right: The parcel pilot counts delivery as successful only if all recipients receive their packages no later than 48 hours after dispatch.
pairs.label_reason: Same population, success condition and time anchor expressed differently.

pairs.left: I postpone the accounting release whenever a failing test could let customers lose saved invoices.
pairs.right: If a test failure puts stored customer invoices at risk, my rule is to delay shipping the accounting update.
pairs.label_reason: Both statements apply the same release rule under the same condition.

pairs.left: Campaign Alpha aims for 10000 advertisement views this month; repeated views by the same person count separately.
pairs.right: Campaign Beta aims for 10000 unique paying customers this month; repeated purchases by one person count once.
pairs.label_reason: Both are campaign targets, but views and unique paying customers are different metrics in separate campaigns.

pairs.left: The north-campus workshop aims to train 200 school teachers in spreadsheet skills by December.
pairs.right: The south-campus workshop aims to train 200 hospital nurses in spreadsheet skills by December.
pairs.label_reason: Training topic and count match, but the beneficiaries and workshop scopes differ.

pairs.left: The coastal nursery project targets planting 500 seedlings by 30 June 2027.
pairs.right: The inland nursery project targets planting 500 seedlings by 31 December 2027.
pairs.label_reason: Related planting goals with different scopes and deadlines do not contradict each other.

pairs.left: The network team will switch the production server to a new routing table during maintenance.
pairs.right: The dining room team will switch the wooden table to the corner before dinner service.
pairs.label_reason: Shared words such as switch, table and service refer to unrelated activities.

pairs.left: This Saturday's entire event budget is 100 dollars with no borrowing. The indoor plan spends 70 dollars from that budget.
pairs.right: For the same Saturday event and the same fixed 100-dollar budget, the outdoor plan spends 60 dollars. Running both plans requires paying both full costs.
pairs.label_reason: Executing both plans would exceed the explicit shared budget; neither plan alone exceeds it.

pairs.left: Issuing an active warehouse access badge to a worker unlocks that worker's gate access.
pairs.right: The worker's intended next step is entering the warehouse through its badge-controlled gate.
pairs.label_reason: Issuing the badge enables the stated entry action through the described gate mechanism.

pairs.left: The operations team's goal is to run the new inventory reports on workstation C.
pairs.right: Installing the licensed reporting application on workstation C makes running those inventory reports possible.
pairs.label_reason: The installation in the right passage enables the report-running goal in the left passage.

pairs.left: Closing the only loading dock for resurfacing blocks all truck loading there until the work finishes.
pairs.right: The dispatch team plans to load trucks at that dock while the resurfacing work is underway.
pairs.label_reason: The closure explicitly obstructs loading at the same place during the same time.

pairs.left: The safety sign-off is the inspector's clearance after checking this bridge.
pairs.right: Reopening this bridge to traffic is permitted only after that safety sign-off; clearance is mandatory.
pairs.label_reason: Reopening on the right requires the sign-off defined on the left, rather than the reverse.

pairs.left: The project log says that it changed after they adjusted that thing, without identifying the thing or the change.
pairs.right: A second project note says that the result may matter to the plan, but does not identify the result, plan or mechanism.
pairs.label_reason: Unresolved referents prevent a grounded determination of the pair's relationship.
